suggestions.text: At Cascade, developers spend about 30% of their time on models and the rest negotiating land leases, interconnection, and offtake contracts. That suggests the role is weighted toward commercial deal-making, though you still don’t know how this split varies across projects or development stages.

Most Cascade developers live in Denver or Boulder, but two work remotely from Durango. This shows a mountain-town arrangement exists at Cascade, though it’s still unclear whether those remote roles are available to new hires or interns.
Cascade usually hires two MBA interns and makes its decision by mid-January.
Priya offered to introduce you to Luis Ortega, who runs Cascade’s storage team.
Send Priya your resume this week.
Read up on the interconnection queue before your next conversation with Priya.

At Basecamp, project managers spend two or three days a week on site during the building season, so the role includes substantial field work. This answers the field-versus-office question for that season; how the schedule changes outside the building season remains unknown.
Sam said Basecamp pay is lower than energy but includes profit sharing. The size of the pay gap and the potential value of profit sharing are still unknown.
Basecamp gets most of its money from towns and counties using public grants, so project timing depends on when grants come through.
Sam would consider a summer MBA fellow if the fellow could own grant applications for two projects.
Send Sam a one-page note outlining how you would approach the grant pipeline.
